name: Interceptor
summary: Lets services be added to a framework transparently, and triggered automatically when particular events occur.

reference.author: Douglas Schmidt, Michael Stal, Hans Rohnert, Frank Buschmann

roles.name: Interceptor
roles.summary: Declares the event-handling hook the framework calls out through. Its implementations are not called by the application at all, which is what makes their effects hard to trace from a stack trace and worth annotating.

roles.name: ConcreteInterceptor
roles.summary: Implements the hook for the events it has subscribed to. It runs on the framework's path rather than the application's, so the cost of what it does is paid by every request the framework handles and attributed to none of them.

roles.name: Dispatcher
roles.summary: Registers and removes interceptors and delegates events to them. Its registration order is the order the interceptors run in, and that order is a decision nothing else records.

roles.name: Context
roles.summary: Carries the information about the event that the interceptor may read, and through which it may change what the framework does next. It is the whole of the interceptor's authority, so what it exposes is what the framework has agreed to let an outsider decide.

roles.name: Framework
roles.summary: The thing being intercepted: it accepts interceptors, keeps them, and calls out to them at the points it has chosen to open. Those points are an interface as real as any method signature, and are the part of a framework that cannot be changed quietly.
